boundary_rationale: Onset at 12:1 with Περὶ δὲ τῶν πνευματικῶν (rp:1Cor.12.1), a peri de (transliterated gloss) topic heading. That the heading answers a matter raised by the addressees is INFERRED from 7:1, the one verse in either witness that names their letter, and from the recurring peri de openings, since 12:1 itself names no letter. The disclosure formula οὐ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν (rp:1Cor.12.1) stands in the same verse at 12:1 and confirms a fresh start. On the far side, 11:34 ends with Τὰ δὲ λοιπά, ὡς ἂν ἔλθω, διατάξομαι (rp:1Cor.11.34), deferring the remaining supper matters to a visit. Inside, Διὸ γνωρίζω ὑμῖν (rp:1Cor.12.3) at 12:3 draws a consequence from the reminder of former idol worship. Close after 12:3: at 12:4 Διαιρέσεις δὲ χαρισμάτων (rp:1Cor.12.4) turns to the distribution of gifts.

The phrase is a refrain, not a frame, because it sounds inside the unit as well: κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα (rp:1Cor.12.8) and ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ πνεύματι (rp:1Cor.12.9), the latter twice in RP, where the second instance in SBL is ἐν τῷ ⸀ἑνὶ πνεύματι (sbl:1Cor.12.9). The close rests on πάντα δὲ ταῦτα (rp:1Cor.12.11), which gathers the list, and on the change of image at 12:12. Close after 12:11: 12:12 opens the body analogy with Καθάπερ γὰρ (rp:1Cor.12.12).

boundary_rationale: Onset at 12:12 with Καθάπερ γὰρ (rp:1Cor.12.12), where body and member vocabulary enters chapter 12 (MEASURED by a token search of 12:1-12:12 in both witnesses). boundary_rationale: Onset at 13:4, where Ἡ ἀγάπη μακροθυμεῖ (rp:1Cor.13.4) begins a chain of predicates with love as repeated subject. At 13:4-13:6 the verbs run two positive, then eight negated, then one positive (MEASURED by a count of the negators in both witnesses). The chain reaches a fourfold cadence at 13:7, where πάντα στέγει (rp:1Cor.13.7) heads four clauses built on panta (transliterated gloss). At 13:8 Ἡ ἀγάπη οὐδέποτε ἐκπίπτει (rp:1Cor.13.8) restates love as subject and turns to permanence set against gifts that cease.

boundary_rationale: Onset at 13:8 with Ἡ ἀγάπη οὐδέποτε ἐκπίπτει (rp:1Cor.13.8), setting the permanence of love against prophecies, tongues and knowledge, which pass. The partial-versus-complete contrast runs through 13:9-13:12 and turns on ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ τὸ τέλειον (rp:1Cor.13.10) at 13:10. The mirror image at 13:12 follows: Βλέπομεν γὰρ ἄρτι δι’ ἐσόπτρου ἐν αἰνίγματι (rp:1Cor.13.12). The close at 13:13 is the triad Νυνὶ δὲ μένει πίστις, ἐλπίς, ἀγάπη (rp:1Cor.13.13), crowned by love. At 14:1 Διώκετε τὴν ἀγάπην (rp:1Cor.14.1) resumes exhortation on the basis of the inset.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the inset at 13:12 and joining 13:13 to 14:1 would treat the triad as a bridge to the pursuit of love. The triad answers the partial-versus-complete contrast and names love as greater, so it closes the inset, and 14:1 restarts with the verse-initial, connective-free Διώκετε (rp:1Cor.14.1).

boundary_rationale: Onset at 14:1 with Διώκετε τὴν ἀγάπην (rp:1Cor.14.1). The same verse continues with ζηλοῦτε δὲ τὰ πνευματικά (rp:1Cor.14.1), taking up the exhortation of 12:31 after the inset. boundary_rationale: Onset at 14:13 with Διόπερ (rp:1Cor.14.13) and the instruction that a tongue-speaker pray for interpretation. boundary_rationale: Onset at 14:26 with Τί οὖν ἐστίν, ἀδελφοί (rp:1Cor.14.26), a vocative question that turns from argument to orderly practice. The governing principle stands in the same verse: Πάντα πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν γινέσθω (rp:1Cor.14.26). Orders for tongues and prophecy follow at 14:27-14:32, closing on καὶ πνεύματα προφητῶν προφήταις ὑποτάσσεται (rp:1Cor.14.32). At 14:33 the ground is given: Οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἀκαταστασίας ὁ θεός, ἀλλὰ εἰρήνης (rp:1Cor.14.33). The verse continues with ὡς ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῶν ἁγίων (rp:1Cor.14.33), and that clause is attached backward here to the ground it illustrates. Close after 14:33: at 14:34 a new subject enters without a connective.

boundary_rationale: Onset at 14:34 with Αἱ γυναῖκες ὑμῶν ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις (rp:1Cor.14.34): a new subject enters without a connective after the ground stated in 14:33. At 14:34 SBL reads Αἱ ⸀γυναῖκες ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις (sbl:1Cor.14.34), omitting the possessive. The instruction continues in 14:35 with Εἰ δέ τι μαθεῖν θέλουσιν (rp:1Cor.14.35). At 14:36 the double question Ἢ ἀφ’ ὑμῶν ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ἐξῆλθεν (rp:1Cor.14.36) challenges the addressees and is attached backward here, as a retort that closes the instruction; this attachment is INFERRED. Close after 14:36: 14:37 opens a conditional with Εἴ τις δοκεῖ προφήτης εἶναι (rp:1Cor.14.37).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 14:36 forward to the conditional of 14:37 is the rival, reading the questions as the opening of a closing challenge to self-styled prophets. The questions address the assembly as a whole with second-person plurals, while 14:37 narrows to anyone who thinks himself a prophet, so 14:36 is kept with the instruction as a soft judgment left open, and the recurrence of ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις (rp:1Cor.14.33) and ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις (rp:1Cor.14.34) on either side of the onset is weighed as a tie that pulls toward 14:33 but does not displace the new subject at 14:34 (INFERRED).

device_notes: Variant sites at 14:34: SBL reads ⸀ἐπιτρέπεται (sbl:1Cor.14.34) where RP has ἐπιτέτραπται (rp:1Cor.14.34). SBL also reads ⸀ὑποτασσέσθωσαν (sbl:1Cor.14.34) at 14:34 where RP has ὑποτάσσεσθαι (rp:1Cor.14.34). At 14:35 SBL marks ⸀μαθεῖν (sbl:1Cor.14.35) and orders the closing clause as ⸂λαλεῖν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ⸃ (sbl:1Cor.14.35), where RP has ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ λαλεῖν (rp:1Cor.14.35). 14:40 holds a further SBL variant site with πάντα ⸀δὲ (sbl:1Cor.14.40). Some witnesses reportedly set 14:34-14:35 after 14:40; that Western transposition is REPORTED at strategy section 4, its witnesses UNAVAILABLE there, and it gives no seam reason. The 14:33b clause may instead head this instruction, and that forward attachment is disclosed with the preceding unit as well. Two word links run against the cut at 14:33/14:34: σιγάτω (rp:1Cor.14.28) at 14:28 and σιγάτω (rp:1Cor.14.30) at 14:30 return as σιγάτωσαν (rp:1Cor.14.34), and ὑποτάσσεται (rp:1Cor.14.32) returns as ὑποτάσσεσθαι (rp:1Cor.14.34). Debates over ordination divide over the instruction at 14:34-14:35 (REPORTED, strategy section 7 B naming hardness_batch_03); its readings and holders are UNAVAILABLE, and no preference between them is taken here. At 14:35 RP has γυναιξὶν (rp:1Cor.14.35) where SBL has γυναικὶ (sbl:1Cor.14.35). Apart from the elided adversative at 14:34, where the two editions word 14:34-14:35 differently both wordings are given: Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine Textform (Unlicense); SBLGNT (CC BY 4.0).

boundary_rationale: Onset at 14:37 with Εἴ τις δοκεῖ προφήτης εἶναι (rp:1Cor.14.37). The conditional addresses anyone claiming prophetic or spiritual standing, who must acknowledge ἃ γράφω ὑμῖν (rp:1Cor.14.37) as a command of the Lord. The sanction follows at 14:38 with Εἰ δέ τις ἀγνοεῖ (rp:1Cor.14.38). At 14:39 Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί, ζηλοῦτε τὸ προφητεύειν (rp:1Cor.14.39) brings back the verb seen at 12:31 and 14:1 and gathers up the chapter's comparison of prophecy and tongues; the directive force of its two verbs is a matter of interpretation and not of measurement (INFERRED), and so taken, prophecy is to be sought eagerly, and speaking in tongues is not to be hindered. Then 14:40 closes with πάντα εὐσχημόνως καὶ κατὰ τάξιν γινέσθω (rp:1Cor.14.40). At 15:1 Γνωρίζω δὲ ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί (rp:1Cor.15.1) introduces the gospel tradition with a disclosure formula.
